'''Ayhan Ulubelen''' (20 August 1931 – 29 November 2020) was a Turkish analytical chemist. She was a member of the [[Turkish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Kurucu Üyemiz Ayhan Ulubelen'i Kaybettik (1931-2020) |date=30 November 2020 |url=https://bilimakademisi.org/kurucu-uyemiz-ayhan-ulubeleni-kaybettik-19312020/ |publisher=Bilim Akademisi |access-date=8 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bilimakademisi.org/independent-science-academy-turkey |title=An Independent Science Academy Founded in Turkey |publisher=Bilim Akademisi |date=2011-08-27 |access-date=2013-07-09 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130630013709/http://www.bilimakademisi.org/independent-science-academy-turkey |archive-date=2013-06-30 }}</ref> Ulubelen contributed to the isolation and testing of [[natural products]] from Turkish plants relevant to spontaneous abortion, cancer, HIV, and diabetes.

==Life and career==
Ulubelen was born August 20, 1931, in [[Istanbul, Turkey]]. Her father was an army officer, and her mother was a housewife. In high school, she saw a movie about [[Madame Curie]] and soon wanted to be a [[chemist]]. {{citation needed|date=July 2013}} She sought a position in chemical industry, but became analytical chemist at the Faculty of Pharmacy of [[Istanbul University]],{{when|date=July 2013}} partly through her having passed the language examination.{{citation needed|date=July 2013}}

She received her degree{{clarify|date=July 2013}} in analytical chemistry at Istanbul University in 1956, followed by two years of postdoctoral research at the [[University of Minnesota]] under Dr. Ole Gisvold (head of the Dept. of Medicinal Chemistry) and then by four years of [[cancer research]] at the [[University of Arizona]]. In 1976, she became a full professor at Istanbul University, while spending several months at each of: Japan (support by [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science|JSPS]]), Germany (support by [[German Academic Exchange Service|DAAD]]), and the [[University of Texas|University of Texas at Austin]] (support by [[NATO]]).

Ulubelen has published more than 300 papers, and has authored two books and 12 chapters in international books; her work has received support from [[Fulbright]], NIH, DAAD, JSPS, and NATO. She has mentored over 20 graduate students, of whom many have proceeded to prominent positions{{citation needed|date=July 2013}} in academia, as well as pharmaceutical and chemical companies.

Ulubelen died from [[COVID-19]] on 29 November 2020, at the age of 89.<ref>[https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/haber/ttb-bir-haftada-20-saglik-calisani-hayatini-kaybetti-1794955 TTB: Bir haftada 20 sağlık çalışanı hayatını kaybetti]</ref>

==Research==
Ulubelen's research focuses on isolation, structure determination, and pharmacological investigation of Turkish plants and compounds isolated from them, and especially on isolates from plants abundant in Turkey and mentioned in Turkish folklore and medicine. Her work with [[triterpenes]] and [[flavonoids]] was followed by work on diterpenoids, to find plant components that produce various medical effects including [[spontaneous abortion]]{{specify|date=May 2012}} and wound healing.{{specify|date=May 2012}}

During tests on mice, Ulubelen found an abortive factor developing cystic degeneration in the ovaries,{{clarify|date=May 2012}} but was unsure whether the effect was caused by the abortive agent or by some other compound. Ten compounds from the source plant were studied, including screening by a Faculty of Medicine group for toxic effects to the ovaries, livers, kidneys, and brain. At that time, Ulubelen said
<blockquote>
"...we can't recommend that women should be using these plants as an abortive agent. We have so informed the pharmacist who sent them to us, and I'm sure she's passing this information on to the villagers."<ref>{{cite book|last=Imperial College Press|title=Hargittai, Candid Science|year=2000|publisher=World Scientific Publishing Co. Pte. Ltd.|location=London|isbn=1-86094-151-6|pages=114–121}}</ref>
</blockquote>

[[3-Benzoxepin]] does not occur naturally but is the skeletal [[moiety (chemistry)|moiety]] around which several [[natural products]] are built, including [[perilloxin]] '''(I)''' from [[Perilla frutescens var. crispa|''Perilla frutescens'' var. ''crispa'']]<ref>{{cite journal|first1 = J.-H.|last1 = Liu|first2 = A.|last2 = Steigel|first3 = E.|last3 = Reininger|first4 = R.|last4 = Bauer|title = Two new prenylated 3-benzoxepin derivatives as cyclooxygenase inhibitors from ''Perilla frutescens'' var. ''acuta''|journal = [[J. Nat. Prod.]]|volume = 63|issue = 3|pages = 403–405|year = 2000|doi = 10.1021/np990362o|pmid = 10757731}}</ref> and [[tenual]] '''(II)''' and [[tenucarb]] '''(III)''' from ''[[Asphodeline tenuior]]'', which Ulubelen helped to isolate.<ref>{{cite journal|first1 = A.|last1 = Ulubelen|author-link1 = Ayhan Ulubelen|first2 = E.|last2 = Tuzlaci|first3 = N.|last3 = Atilan|title = Oxepine derivatives and anthraquinones from ''Asphodeline tenuior'' and ''A. taurica''|journal = [[Phytochemistry (journal)|Phytochemistry]]|volume = 28|issue = 2|pages = 649–650|year = 1989|doi = 10.1016/0031-9422(89)80076-7| bibcode=1989PChem..28..649U }}</ref>

==Honors==
Ulubelen's honors include: Honorary Membership to the Chemical Society of Turkey (first award recipient, 1985), NATO Scientific Committee membership (selected from among ten NATO countries, 1986–1990), Science Award by the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey (1991), full member (1994–2001) and honorary member of the Turkish Academy of Sciences (2001-2020), and the American Pharmaceutical Association Young Scientist awards (1962, 1963, 1964). She has served in the Chemrawn Committee of IUPAC as an associate and full member (2003–2009).<ref>{{cite web|title=New Challenges in Natural Products Chemistry |url=http://www.specialconference-ulubelen.org/aulubelen.asp |work=Conference in honour of Prof. Dr. Ayhan Ulubelen |publisher=International Year of Chemistry 2011 |access-date=April 23, 2012 }}{{dead link|date=October 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
